collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder potter or an elder and a young adult, 18-25; in the story (name1)'s hands shake)

collection.description: An elder potter's hands shake, and the apprentice keeps smoothing the wavy rims: ask them to stop, or let them help.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s hands have started to shake, a fine tremor that never quite stops. (subject.He/she) still makes pots, every day, but the rims come out wavy now, and the patterns wobble. (friend), (subject.his/her) apprentice, has started quietly smoothing the rims before they dry, trying to make them straight again.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Leave them," says (subject). "That's what they look like now." (friend) protests. (subject) holds one up to the light, the wavy rim like a little sea. "I've made straight pots for forty years. These ones are mine too." (friend) leaves them. People start asking for "the wavy ones" by name. (subject) is quietly very pleased.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) lets (friend) help with the rims, and they work out a way to do it together: (subject) shapes, (friend) steadies. The pots come out somewhere between (subject)'s old ones and the new wavy ones. They're good pots. (subject) misses doing it alone sometimes. (subject.He/she) also likes the company more than (subject.he/she) expected.
